records.title: Need to restore the storage capacity of Khadakwasla dam and strengthen Puneâ€™s water security.
details:
Dr. MedhaVishram Kulkarni: 
I seek to draw attention of the Government to the serious and
long-term challenge posed by the declining storage capacity of the Khadakwasla
Dam, which remains the principal source of water supply for Pune city and
several adjoining areas. Recent assessments indicate that the dam, originally
designed to store approximately 3.75 TMC of water, has lost more than half of
its effective storage capacity due to decades of silt accumulation. As a
result, its current holding capacity has reportedly reduced to nearly 1.75 TMC.
This substantial loss of storage has weakened the reservoir?s ability to
conserve water during the monsoon and meet growing urban demand during dry
periods. Pune is one of India?s fastest-growing metropolitan regions, with
increasing requirements for drinking water, industry, public services and
environmental sustainability. The reduced carrying capacity of the reservoir
places immense pressure on water management authorities, particularly during
years of deficient rainfall. It also raises concerns regarding long-term water
resilience and the adequacy of existing storage and distribution systems.
I
urge the Government to coordinate with the concerned authorities to examine
measures such as scientific desilting, catchment area treatment, sediment
management, reservoir modernisation and improved water budgeting. A
comprehensive assessment of the Khadakwasla reservoir system and its future
sustainability is essential to safeguard the water security of millions of
citizens. Water security is central to urban development, public health
and economic growth. Timely intervention today will help prevent a far more
serious crisis in the years ahead.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over decline in water quality of Mula–Mutha Rivers in Pune.
details:
Dr. MedhaVishram Kulkarni:
?I draw attention
of the Government to the deterioration in the water quality of the Mula?Mutha
river system in Pune, as highlighted in a study conducted by the Central Water
and Power Research Station (CWRPRS) under the National Hydrology Project of the
Ministry of Jal Shakti. The report states that while flowing through Pune city,
the Mula and Mutha rivers are the most vulnerable due to untreated sewage
discharge, pollution, narrowing of the riverbed, encroachments on floodplains
and inadequate environmental flow, adversely affecting river ecology, public
health and urban water sustainability. Pune generates nearly 900 million litres
of sewage every day, of which only about 600 million litres is treated before
discharge into the rivers. Although eleven sewage treatment plants with a
combined capacity of 396 million litres have been proposed, the report notes
delays in implementation, resulting in a substantial treatment gap. The CWRPRS
study also undertook computational flood modelling, warning that riverbed
constriction and floodplain encroachments significantly increase flood risks
during heavy rainfall. The report further emphasizes maintaining adequate
dissolved oxygen levels and minimum ecological flow to restore water quality
and aquatic life. Despite submission of this report to the Pune Municipal
Corporation, effective on-ground action remains inadequate.
??????????? 
??????????? I urge the Government, in
coordination with the State Government and local authorities, to ensure
time-bound implementation of the recommendations, strict monitoring of sewage
discharge, protection of floodplains and restoration of the Mula?Mutha rivers
in the larger public interest.
??????????? (ENDS)

records.title: Demand for Inclusion of Alandi under the Temple Town Development Framework.
Concerns regarding unfair rejection and delay in health insurance claim settlements by private insurance companies.
details:
Dr. MedhaVishram Kulkarni: 
I seek to draw attention of the Government
to the growing concern regarding the increasing instances of delay and unjust
rejection of health insurance claims by certain private insurance companies,
causing serious hardship to policyholders across the country. Private insurers
promote health policies with promises of cashless treatment and quick
settlement of claims. Yet, during medical emergencies many families later find
their claims partially approved, delayed, or rejected on technical grounds such
as pre-existing disease clauses, documentation issues, or restrictive policy
conditions. According to the latest annual report of the Insurance Regulatory
and Development Authority of India, nearly 2.57 lakh complaints were registered
in the insurance sector during 2024?25, including about 1.22 lakh related to
claim settlement disputes, a large share from health insurance. Policyholders
have also raised concerns regarding the practices of certain insurers where
delays, repeated document requests, and prolonged verification processes create
difficulties for patients and hospitals. In many cases, patients enter
hospitals expecting insurance coverage, but at the time of discharge, families
have to arrange large payments due to unresolved claims, placing severe
financial and emotional pressure on ordinary citizens. I therefore urge the
Government to strengthen regulatory oversight, ensure strict action against
insurers unfairly rejecting claims, mandate dedicated claim-settlement managers
to coordinate with hospitals, require transparent disclosure of policy terms
before sale, and ensure that all insurance-related complaints are resolved
within a fixed time frame of 30 days to protect policyholders and maintain
public confidence in the health insurance system.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over circulation of AI-generated and morphed obscene content of Hindu Gods and Goddesses on social media.
details:
Dr. Medha Vishram Kulkarni: I wish to draw the
attention of the Government to a deeply disturbing and sensitive issue. 
In recent months, social media platforms and several internet sites have
witnessed a surge in AI-generated, morphed and deepfake nude and obscene images
and videos of Hindu Gods and Goddesses. Reports indicate that a large number of
Hindu deities are being deliberately and systematically targeted by certain
miscreants with malicious intent, clearly aimed at hurting religious
sentiments, provoking communal tension, and destabilising social harmony across
the country. The misuse of AI, deepfake tools and sophisticated
image-manipulation technologies has opened dangerous new front in cybercrime.
Religious icons and sacred imagery are being distorted and circulated with
impunity, revealing not only inadequacy of current legal frameworks but also
urgent need for stronger accountability mechanisms for digital platforms. The
scale, coordination and intent behind these activities show a planned attempt
to malign Hindu faith and undermine cultural unity. In this context, I urge the
Government to take following steps:1. Launch immediate, strict and exemplary
action against those creating or circulating such offensive content;
2. Mandate social media companies to deploy proactive
AI-based detection, swift takedown systems, and stricter verification protocols
for sensitive content; 3. Formulate a strong and comprehensive ?Hindu Faith
Protection Law / Anti-Blasphemy Law? with stringent provisions against
AI-enabled religious defamation; 4. Establish a special cyber task force
dedicated to religious desecration cases. Protecting our faith, cultural
dignity and societal harmony is our collective constitutional responsibility. I
request intervention from the Government in the matter.
(ENDS)

Need for Cancer prevention and treatment measures in rural areas of Maharashtra.
details:
Dr. Medha Vishram
Kulkarni: I
rise to draw the attention of Government to an alarming public health concern
emerging from Hingoli district in Maharashtra. During? recent Sanjivani health
screening campaign, over 14,500 women were found with symptoms suggestive of Cancer
out of approximately 2.93 lakh women screened.
This situation underscores the critical
need for early detection, timely diagnosis, and accessible treatment,
especially in rural and underserved regions. While such mass screening
campaigns are laudable, they must be strengthened with robust follow-up
mechanisms and medical infrastructure. ????????? I urge the Government to
consider the following immediate measures:1. Establish and upgrade diagnostic
facilities at local health centers for mammography, cervical screening and
biopsy services.2. Deploy mobile oncology units in remote areas to ensure
on-ground diagnosis and early-stage intervention. 3. Launch targeted awareness
drives to educate women about early warning signs and remove the stigma
associated with Cancer. 4. Leverage schemes such as Ayushman Bharat and Mahatma
Jyotiba Phule Jan Arogya Yojana to cover diagnostic tests and treatment
comprehensively. ?????? Maharashtra reported the second-highest number of Cancer
cases in India in 2023, with around 1.21 lakh new cases, a rise from 1.18 lakh
in 2021. These numbers reflect a growing cancer burden in the State,
particularly among the women in rural areas. This is a silent crisis that requires
a multi-sectoral, urgent and sustained response. I request the Government to
ensure that early detection leads to timely care and positive outcomes for
every woman affected.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over Aadhaar access issues for biometrically unfit citizens.
details:
Dr. MedhaVishram Kulkarni: I rise to draw
the attention of the Government to an urgent and deeply concerning issue
affecting thousands across our country. There are countless citizens
particularly senior citizens, persons with disabilities, manual labourers,
farmers and those in rural and remote areas who are unable to authenticate
their Aadhaar due to worn-out fingerprints, retinal damage or physical
impairments. Many also suffer from chronic health conditions that prevent
biometric verification. As a result, they are being denied access to essential
services such as food rations under PDS, old age pensions, healthcare benefits
and even banking.While UIDAI does provide for ?exceptional enrolment? and
alternative mechanisms such as facial recognition and OTP-based authentication,
these alternatives are not being implemented effectively at the grassroots.
Frontline staff are often unaware or unwilling to facilitate such cases.? I
urge the Government to take the following steps on priority:?Implement
alternative Aadhaar authentication methods in mission mode; ?Ensure no citizen
is denied access to welfare due to biometric mismatch;?Launch a nationwide
awareness campaign and establish dedicated grievance redressal systems; and ?Appoint
a nodal officer in each district to ensure easy access and swift resolution. I
urge the Government to look into this matter.
(ENDS)

records.title: Urgent demand for direct train services from Pune to Nashik
details:
Smt.
Medha Vishram Kulkarni: I rise today to draw the attention of this august House to the
urgent need for a direct train service between Pune Junction and Nashik,
primarily to facilitate the travel of devotees visiting the Kalamandir, a
revered temple of Lord Ram in Nashik. Nashik holds profound significance in
Hindu mythology as the place where Lord Ram had spent part of his exile. The
Kalamandir attracts thousands of devotees from across India. However, the
absence of a direct train link from Pune, a major urban center, poses
significant inconvenience. Currently, travellers from Pune must either change
trains at Manmad or rely on bus services to reach Nashik. This indirect route
not only extends the journey time but also increases costs and discomfort,
especially for elderly devotees and economically weaker sections. Introducing
direct train service between Pune and Nashik would significantly improve access
to the Kalamandir, thereby boosting religious tourism in the region. This
initiative would reflect the governments commitment to preserving and
promoting Indias rich cultural heritage. Furthermore, establishing this train
route would create employment opportunities and spur economic development in
the local areas. It would also stand as a testament to the governments
dedication to facilitating the spiritual and cultural journeys of its citizens.
Therefore, I urge Hon?ble Railway Minister to consider the immediate initiation
of direct train services from Pune Junction to Nashik. This move would not only
meet the needs of the devotees but also underscore the governments commitment
to upholding cultural values and ensuring public welfare.
(Ends)

records.title: Demand to increase frequency of trains and reduce crowd in Mumbai suburban local trains
details:
Dr.
Medha Vishram Kulkarni: I rise to draw the attention of this august House to the pressing
issue of overcrowding in the Mumbai suburban local train network and the urgent
need to increase train frequency to prevent accidents. Mumbai?s suburban
railway, catering to over 7.5 million commuters daily, is the lifeline of the
city. However, the current infrastructure is severely strained, leading to
perilous conditions for passengers.
According
to recent data, over 2,000 deaths and nearly 3,000 injuries were reported on
the suburban railway network in 2023 due to overcrowding-related accidents. The
peak hours witness trains operating at over 300% capacity, with passengers
risking their lives by hanging onto doors and windows. Such overcrowding not
only endangers lives but also severely impacts the quality of life and
productivity of millions of Mumbaikars.
There
is an urgent need to increase the frequency of trains during peak hours.
Currently, the Central and Western lines run trains at intervals of
approximately 3-5 minutes. By increasing the frequency to 2-3 minutes, the load
can be significantly reduced. Additionally, deploying more 15-coach trains,
instead of the current 12-coach ones, can accommodate more passengers per trip.
I
urge the Ministry of Railways to prioritize this issue and allocate necessary
funds and resources for infrastructure upgrades. This includes expediting the
ongoing Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP) phases and ensuring timely
completion. Enhancing the suburban train network will not only save lives but
also improve the overall efficiency and reliability of Mumbai?s public
transport system.
(Ends)
